title: introduce-ci-operator-gate-and-shard-test-lanes-to-speed-feedback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Our single-path CI (monolithic lint -> unit -> integration -> release smoke) has grown slow and brittle. Developers hit 10+ minute feedback loops for trivial lint or dependency changes, and dependency churn has caused transient infra failures that block work. This PR introduces a lightweight CI operator gate and sharded fast-feedback lanes to reduce iteration time while preserving safety for release branches.

What this PR does (high-level): - Add a small, idempotent CI operator job (scripts/ci/operator_gate.py + action) that validates dependency snapshots, checks action SHAs, and gates heavy pipelines on a preflight pass. The operator also tags PRs with "fastpath-eligible" when only safe files change. - Split the default workflow into three lanes: fastpath (lint + unit tests + dep-scan, targeted), runtime-sharded integration (integration tests split by runtime: runtime/cpu, runtime/gpu, runtime/quant), and full-nightly (heavy e2e and long-running sanity). Fastpath runs in <6m for most changes. - Move lint to a hermetic container image (tools/lint-runner) to reduce flakiness from host variations and cached node_modules. - Introduce a dependency-snapshot manifest (build/dep-snapshot.yaml) and an action that verifies package-lock / yarn.lock / go.sum consistency against the snapshot on PRs touching dependency files. - Pin a small set of composite actions and add an action-sha verifier to CI operator to reduce surprising upstream action changes. - Add small UX: GitHub PR comment bot summarizing which lane ran, and clear rerun instructions for flaky integration shards.

Why this is different from prior CI refactors: Rather than stitching more steps into the same monolith, this change introduces an operator/gate coupled with explicit fast/slow lanes and a small amount of metadata on PRs to decide routing. The aim is to cut developer wait time for ordinary changes while keeping a conservative path to catch regressions for releases.

Commits (summary): - commit 1: add ci operator script, basic verification and labeling - commit 2: split workflows into .github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml and ci-sharded-integration.yml - commit 3: add tools/lint-runner Dockerfile and hermetic lint entrypoint - commit 4: dependency snapshot manifest and lockfile verifier action - commit 5: pin composite actions and add action-sha-verifier - commit 6: PR comment reporter and docs updates in docs/ci/fast-feedback.md

Files changed (high level examples): - .github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml (new) - .github/workflows/ci-sharded-integration.yml (new) - .github/workflows/ci-nightly.yml (tweaks) - .github/actions/operator/entrypoint.sh (new small wrapper) - scripts/ci/operator_gate.py (new) - tools/lint-runner/Dockerfile (+entrypoint.sh) - build/dep-snapshot.yaml (new manifest) - docs/ci/fast-feedback.md (new doc) - package.json / go.mod touched in a couple of microservices (to update lock verification flow)

Testing and CI behavior: Initial run: fastpath showed ~40% reduction in median feedback time. On the first CI run, dep-scan failed due to two packages missing a checksum in our snapshot; fixed in commit 4. Integration shards were flaky on the first run (gpu shard timed out); added a retry wrapper and lowered parallelism for the GPU shard which stabilized subsequent runs. CI check matrix summary: - fastpath (lint, unit, dep-scan): pass - integration-shards (cpu, gpu, quant): cpu: pass, gpu: flaky->pass after retries, quant: pass - nightly/long-e2e: unchanged and scheduled - action-sha-verifier: flagged two out-of-date composite actions (pinned them).

Review conversation (abridged, included in the PR body for audit): - Arjun Rao (reviewer): "High-level: love the operator approach. Two asks: 1) can we document the exact criteria for fastpath-eligible files? 2) the operator scripts should be idempotent and not race the label bot." - Maya (author): "Answered: added explicit path patterns in docs/ci/fast-feedback.md and added a tiny ledger file in /tmp on the action runner to avoid duplicate labeling." - Lena Ortiz: "Can you make lint-runner image smaller? The current image is ~600MB; suggested drop build tools and use multi-stage." - Maya: "Addressed via a multi-stage Dockerfile and alpine-based final image, now ~160MB." - Tomás Delgado: "Integration shards look good; please add an alerting threshold for shard flakiness so we can detect regressions." - Maya: "Added a metric export to the console agent for shard-failure-rate (metrics/ci/shard_failure_rate) and configured an alert in SLO tooling (slo/alerts)." - CI bot: initially failed dep-scan -> author fixed and pushed commit, CI retried and passed; reviewers re-approved.

Release notes (user-facing): "Developer CI: reduced median PR feedback time by introducing a fastpath CI lane and an operator gate that validates dependency snapshots and action SHAs. Lint runs use a hermetic runner; integration tests are sharded per runtime. No behavioural changes to production code."

Backwards compatibility and risks: - This is a CI infra change only; does not change runtime or model-serving code. - Risk: new operator adds another moving piece; mitigations: operator logic is intentionally tiny, runs as a read-only verifier for main branches until a 2-week burn-in where it will be allowed to gate by label. - Risk: sharded integrations may hide cross-shard interactions; mitigations: keep nightly full-e2e and add a post-merge job that runs a compact cross-shard smoke set for merged PRs.

Follow-ups (small): - Add a dashboard showing fastpath vs slowpath throughput and median feedback time (ENG-2312). - Migrate a few more repos (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-examples) to the same operator pattern in a follow-up.

Related work: ENG-2241 (CI workstream), ENG-2312 (fast-feedback metrics), and previous CI hygiene PRs that pinned action SHA lists.

Merge: Squash-and-merge after final approvals.
